source_manual.title: Trajectory Analysis and Optimization System (TAOS) User's Manual

exclusion: pure formatting or historical UI behavior unless it affects computation
full parser grammar, which is maintained separately
claims of runtime equivalence without historical executable baselines

algorithms.name: ECFC to ECIC Coordinate Conversion
algorithms.summary: Compute earth rotation angle and transform position, inertial velocity, and inertial acceleration components between ECFC and ECIC descriptions.
assumptions: Earth spin axis is aligned with the ECFC and ECIC z axes.
steps: Evaluate the ECIC-to-ECFC rotation angle from the initial epoch and earth spin rate.
Construct the rotated ECIC x and y unit directions in ECFC components.
Project position onto the ECIC basis.
Add the rotational velocity term before projecting inertial velocity.
Project force divided by mass to obtain inertial acceleration components.
edge_cases: Angle wrapping is arbitrary because sine and cosine are periodic.

unit: Verify zero-rotation identity case.
Verify a 90-degree z rotation.
properties: Preserve position-vector norm.
Rotation basis is orthonormal.
regression: Compare equations 2-3 through 2-5 against direct matrix evaluation.

algorithms.name: Local Geocentric Horizon Unit Vectors
algorithms.summary: Construct local north, east, and down unit vectors from geocentric latitude and longitude.
outputs: local geocentric north/east/down unit vectors in ECFC components
steps: Evaluate sine and cosine of geocentric latitude and longitude.
Assemble north, east, and down basis vectors using equation 2-6.
Return the right-handed orthonormal basis.
edge_cases: At the poles, longitude is geometrically arbitrary but still selects an east direction.

unit: Check equator/Greenwich basis.
Check north-pole limiting basis.
properties: Each vector has unit norm.
Pairwise dot products are zero.
north cross east equals down.

algorithms.name: Geocentric Position to ECFC
algorithms.summary: Convert geocentric radius, longitude, and latitude to ECFC Cartesian position.
steps: Compute the equatorial projection as radius times cosine of latitude.
Resolve the projection into ECFC x and y using longitude.
Compute ECFC z as radius times sine of latitude.

unit: Check equator/Greenwich, 90E, and north-pole points.
properties: Output norm equals input radius.

algorithms.name: ECFC Position to Geocentric Coordinates
algorithms.summary: Recover radius, longitude, and geocentric latitude from an ECFC Cartesian position.
steps: Compute radius from the Euclidean norm.
Compute longitude with a quadrant-aware atan2 of y and x.
Compute geocentric latitude from z and the equatorial projection.
edge_cases: Longitude is undefined on the spin axis; choose the documented numerical convention.

properties: Round-trip with geocentric_position_to_ecfc away from singular points.

algorithms.name: ECFC Velocity to Geocentric Flight-Path Coordinates
algorithms.summary: Convert an earth-relative ECFC velocity vector to speed, geocentric vertical flight-path angle, and heading.
steps: Project velocity onto local north, east, and down directions.
Compute speed from the vector norm.
Recover vertical flight-path angle from the down projection.
Recover heading with atan2 of east and north projections.
edge_cases: If speed is zero, set both angles to zero.
If velocity is vertical, heading is undefined and TAOS sets it to zero.

unit: Check due-north, due-east, vertical-up, and vertical-down velocities.
properties: Round-trip with geocentric_velocity_to_ecfc.

algorithms.name: Geocentric Flight-Path Coordinates to ECFC Velocity
algorithms.summary: Convert speed, geocentric flight-path angle, and heading into an earth-relative ECFC velocity vector.
steps: Resolve speed into local north, east, and down components.
Transform local components to ECFC using longitude and geocentric latitude.
Return the assembled ECFC vector.

properties: Preserve speed norm.
Round-trip with ecfc_velocity_to_geocentric away from angle singularities.

algorithms.name: Ellipsoid Shape-Parameter Conversion
algorithms.summary: Convert among polar radius, eccentricity, flattening, and equatorial radius for the ellipsoidal Earth model.
inputs: one of polar radius, eccentricity, or flattening
outputs: consistent polar radius, eccentricity, and flattening
assumptions: Eccentricity and flattening are less than one.
Polar radius is less than equatorial radius.
steps: Validate the supplied shape parameter.
Use equation 2-18 to compute the two remaining equivalent parameters.
Return a normalized ellipsoid definition.
edge_cases: Spherical Earth has zero eccentricity and flattening.

unit: Check WGS-84 values.
Check spherical limiting case.
properties: Conversions are mutually consistent within tolerance.

algorithms.name: Local Geodetic Horizon Unit Vectors
algorithms.summary: Construct local geodetic north, east, and down unit vectors from geodetic latitude and longitude.
outputs: local geodetic north/east/down basis in ECFC components
steps: Evaluate sine and cosine of geodetic latitude and longitude.
Assemble the three basis vectors from equations 2-19 through 2-21.
Return the right-handed orthonormal basis.
edge_cases: Longitude is arbitrary at the poles.

properties: Unit norms, orthogonality, and handedness.

algorithms.name: Ellipsoidal Surface Geometry
algorithms.summary: Compute prime-vertical geometry used by geodetic position conversion, including the surface normal distance N.
steps: Evaluate the ellipsoid equation in the meridional plane.
Use the surface-normal slope relation to solve for the surface point.
Compute N from equatorial radius, eccentricity, and latitude.
Compute the surface z coordinate and normal-axis offset.

unit: Check equator and pole limits.
properties: Computed surface point satisfies the ellipsoid equation.

algorithms.name: Geodetic Position to ECFC
algorithms.summary: Convert geodetic longitude, latitude, and altitude to an ECFC Cartesian position.
steps: Compute N for the supplied latitude.
Compute equatorial projection (N+h) cos(latitude).
Resolve x and y using longitude.
Compute z using N(1-e^2)+h.

unit: Check equator, pole, and zero-altitude cases.
properties: Round-trip with ecfc_position_to_geodetic.

algorithms.name: ECFC Position to Geodetic Coordinates
algorithms.summary: Iteratively recover geodetic longitude, latitude, and altitude from an ECFC Cartesian position.
steps: Compute longitude from the ECFC equatorial projection.
Initialize the surface-normal z-axis intercept using the nearly spherical approximation.
Repeatedly update the corrected z coordinate, N+h, geodetic latitude, N, and the intercept.
Stop when successive intercept values differ by less than 1e-8 or after 25 iterations.
Recover altitude from N+h and return the geodetic coordinates.

unit: Check documented convergence on typical low-Earth positions.
properties: Round-trip residual below 0.01 ft for representative points.
edge_cases: Poles, high altitude, below-surface positions, and earth center.

algorithms.name: ECFC Velocity to Geodetic Flight-Path Coordinates
algorithms.summary: Convert earth-relative ECFC velocity into speed, geodetic vertical flight-path angle, and heading.
steps: Project velocity onto the geodetic local horizon basis.
Compute speed from the vector norm.
Compute vertical flight-path angle from the down-axis component.
Compute heading from east and north components.
edge_cases: Use the same zero-speed and vertical-flight conventions as the geocentric conversion.

properties: Round-trip with geodetic_velocity_to_ecfc.

algorithms.name: Geodetic Flight-Path Coordinates to ECFC Velocity
algorithms.summary: Convert speed, geodetic vertical flight-path angle, and heading to an earth-relative ECFC velocity vector.
steps: Resolve speed into local geodetic north, east, and down components.
Transform the local components into ECFC components.
Return the ECFC vector.

properties: Preserve speed norm.
Round-trip with ecfc_velocity_to_geodetic.

algorithms.name: Euler Angles to Body-Fixed Basis
algorithms.summary: Apply TAOS yaw, pitch, and roll rotations to construct body-fixed unit vectors from a local horizon or inertial-platform frame.
outputs: body x/y/z unit vectors in ECFC components
steps: Apply yaw about the reference z axis.
Apply pitch about the first intermediate y axis.
Apply roll about the second intermediate x axis.
Expand the composite matrix to obtain body unit vectors.

unit: Check zero angles and individual 90-degree rotations.
properties: Composite basis is orthonormal and right-handed.

algorithms.name: Body-Fixed Basis to Euler Angles
algorithms.summary: Recover yaw, pitch, and roll from body and reference-frame unit vectors using projections and an intermediate axis.
steps: Project the body x axis into the reference horizontal plane to recover yaw.
Project body x onto reference down to recover pitch.
Construct the intermediate y axis perpendicular to body x and reference down.
Project body y onto the intermediate frame to recover roll.
Apply the TAOS vertical-body singularity convention when yaw is undefined.
edge_cases: When body x is vertical, set yaw and roll according to equation 2-61.

properties: Round-trip with euler_angles_to_body_basis away from gimbal singularity.
edge_cases: Body pointed straight up and down.

algorithms.name: Wind-Relative and Earth-Relative Velocity Frames
algorithms.summary: Construct velocity coordinate systems from wind-corrected or earth-relative velocity and express the earth-relative frame through heading and flight-path rotations.
steps: Subtract wind velocity from earth-relative velocity to obtain air-relative velocity.
Normalize the selected velocity vector to obtain the frame x axis.
Use local down and cross products to construct y and z axes.
For the earth-relative frame, alternatively evaluate the heading and flight-path rotation equations.
edge_cases: Zero airspeed makes the wind-relative frame undefined.
Velocity parallel to local down requires a fallback heading convention.

properties: Basis orthonormality.
x axis aligned with selected velocity.
airspeed equals wind-corrected velocity norm.

algorithms.name: Wind, Body, and Aerodynamic Angle Transformations
algorithms.summary: Construct the wind frame from bank angle, construct body attitude from aerodynamic angles, and convert among alpha/beta, Euler sideslip, total angle of attack, and windward meridian representations.
steps: Rotate velocity y/z axes by bank angle to obtain the wind frame.
Apply angle of attack and Euler sideslip to obtain body unit vectors when that pair is supplied.
Use projection definitions for conventional sideslip and windward meridian.
Convert the supplied angle pair into the two remaining representations using equations 2-81 through 2-89.
Apply special definitions at 90-degree angle of attack and at zero total angle of attack.
edge_cases: Wind vector in the body y-z plane.

properties: All angle representations reconstruct the same body basis.
Body and wind bases remain orthonormal.

algorithms.name: Inertial Platform Coordinate Evaluation
algorithms.summary: Project vehicle position relative to a platform origin, inertial velocity, and inertial acceleration onto an inertially fixed platform basis.
outputs: platform-relative position, velocity, and acceleration components
steps: Subtract platform-origin position from vehicle position.
Project relative position onto the platform basis.
Project inertial velocity and inertial acceleration onto the same basis.

unit: Check identity-aligned platform.
properties: Projection agrees with matrix multiplication.

algorithms.name: Tangent-Plane Basis and Coordinates
algorithms.summary: Construct a fixed tangent-plane basis from origin latitude/longitude and azimuth, then project relative position, velocity, and acceleration.
steps: Evaluate tangent-plane x/y/z unit vectors from origin latitude, longitude, and azimuth.
Convert the origin geodetic position to ECFC.
Subtract origin position from vehicle position.
Project relative position, earth-relative velocity, and acceleration onto the tangent basis.

unit: Check north-aligned and east-aligned tangent planes.
properties: Basis orthonormality.
Origin maps to zero position.

algorithms.name: Generic Unit-Vector Coordinate Transformation
algorithms.summary: Transform vector components between ECFC and any TAOS orthonormal frame by dot products or the transpose transformation.
steps: For ECFC-to-frame conversion, take dot products with destination unit vectors.
For frame-to-ECFC conversion, form the linear combination of ECFC-expressed basis vectors.
Exploit orthogonality so the inverse transformation is the transpose.

properties: Forward followed by inverse returns the original vector.
Norm is preserved.

algorithms.name: Rotating-Earth Point-Mass Equations of Motion
algorithms.summary: Compute ECFC acceleration from external force, mass, Coriolis acceleration, and centrifugal acceleration, and express the second-order equation as first-order state equations.
assumptions: The center of Earth is nonaccelerating.
steps: Compute force acceleration as total external force divided by mass.
Compute the Coriolis term -2 omega cross velocity.
Compute the centrifugal term -omega cross (omega cross position).
Sum the three terms to obtain ECFC acceleration.
Return position derivative equal to earth-relative velocity and velocity derivative equal to ECFC acceleration.
edge_cases: Position at Earth center terminates the trajectory.

unit: Check zero-spin reduction to Newton's second law.
properties: Vector and component equations agree.
regression: Reproduce selected Section 2.2 numerical consistency checks.

algorithms.name: State Vector and Derivative Assembly
algorithms.summary: Assemble the six-component ECFC state and derivative vectors and append mass, path-length, ground-range, and user-defined integral states.
steps: Place ECFC position and velocity components in the base state vector.
Evaluate ECFC acceleration components from force and rotation terms.
Append mass, path length, ground range, and configured integral variables.
Append their derivatives: mass rate, speed, ground speed, and user expressions.

unit: Verify component ordering and derivative dimensions.
properties: State and derivative lengths match configured augmented states.

algorithms.name: Fixed-Step Fourth-Order Runge-Kutta Integration
algorithms.summary: Advance the complete state vector one fixed time step using four derivative evaluations and the classical RK4 weighted sum.
steps: Evaluate derivatives at the initial state.
Evaluate derivatives at the midpoint using the first slope.
Evaluate derivatives at the midpoint using the second slope.
Evaluate derivatives at the end using the third slope.
Combine slopes with weights 1, 2, 2, 1 divided by 6.

unit: Integrate constant and exponential derivative models.
properties: Observe fourth-order convergence under step halving.
regression: Match the repository's existing RK4 check.

algorithms.name: Rail Launch and Sled Constraint Model
algorithms.summary: Restrict acceleration to the body x axis and apply static or kinetic rail friction for launch rails and sled tracks.
steps: Project total acceleration onto the body x/rail direction.
Compute the vector acceleration normal to the rail.
Choose static friction below 0.001 ft/s, otherwise kinetic friction.
Subtract friction acceleration from the rail-direction acceleration.
For launch rails, clamp backward acceleration to zero; allow both directions for sleds.
edge_cases: Velocity close to the 0.001 ft/s threshold.

unit: Check horizontal rail before ignition.
Check static-to-kinetic transition.
properties: Final acceleration has no component normal to the rail.

algorithms.name: Longitude and Geocentric Latitude Rates
algorithms.summary: Compute longitude rate from ECFC position and velocity and geocentric latitude rate from the local geocentric north component.
steps: Differentiate the atan2 longitude definition.
Divide the tangential cross term by squared equatorial projection.
Project velocity onto local geocentric north and divide by radius for latitude rate.
edge_cases: If the equatorial projection is zero, TAOS sets longitude rate to zero.

unit: Check equatorial eastward motion and meridional motion.
properties: Finite-difference longitude and latitude agree with analytic rates.

algorithms.name: Geodetic Latitude and Altitude Rates
algorithms.summary: Compute altitude rate and geodetic latitude rate for an ellipsoidal Earth using local geodetic projections and curvature terms.
steps: Evaluate the auxiliary equatorial projection and its derivative.
Project velocity on local geodetic down to obtain altitude rate.
Compute the meridional curvature denominator from N, eccentricity, latitude, and altitude.
Divide the local north velocity component by the curvature denominator.
edge_cases: If the geodetic-rate denominator vanishes, use geocentric latitude rate.

properties: Finite-difference geodetic coordinates agree with analytic rates.

algorithms.name: Geodetic Altitude Acceleration
algorithms.summary: Differentiate geodetic altitude rate, including the time derivative of the local down unit vector, to obtain vertical acceleration.
steps: Differentiate altitude rate as the negative projection of velocity on local down.
Evaluate the time derivative of the geodetic down vector from latitude and longitude rates.
Combine acceleration projection and moving-basis contribution.

properties: Compare against a centered finite difference of altitude rate.

algorithms.name: Dynamic-Pressure Rate and Acceleration
algorithms.summary: Compute density rate and an approximate second derivative of dynamic pressure from atmospheric density gradients and air-relative speed.
assumptions: Second derivative of air-relative velocity is neglected.
Second altitude derivative of density is neglected.
Air-relative acceleration magnitude is approximated by earth-fixed acceleration magnitude.
steps: Evaluate dynamic pressure from density and air-relative speed squared.
Compute density rate using altitude rate and the atmospheric gradient.
Approximate density second derivative using altitude acceleration and the first gradient.
Substitute into equation 2-142 with the documented acceleration approximations.

unit: Check constant-density constant-speed case.
properties: Compare with finite differences for smooth atmosphere profiles within approximation tolerance.

algorithms.name: Mach-Number Rate
algorithms.summary: Differentiate Mach number using air-relative speed, speed-of-sound altitude gradient, and the documented acceleration approximation.
assumptions: Air-relative acceleration magnitude is approximated by earth-fixed acceleration magnitude.
steps: Evaluate Mach number as air-relative speed divided by speed of sound.
Compute speed-of-sound rate from altitude rate and atmospheric gradient.
Apply the quotient derivative in equation 2-146.

properties: Compare with finite differences of Mach for a smooth trajectory state.
edge_cases: Very small speed of sound is invalid.

algorithms.name: Ground Speed and Ground-Range Integration
algorithms.summary: Compute velocity of the geodetic surface point below the vehicle and integrate its magnitude to obtain ground range.
inputs: local geodetic basis and basis rates
steps: Differentiate the altitude vector from the surface point to the vehicle.
Subtract altitude-vector rate from vehicle velocity to obtain surface-point velocity.
Express the result in geodetic flight-path components.
Take the magnitude for ground speed and use it as the ground-range state derivative.

unit: Stationary vehicle has zero ground speed.
Low-altitude horizontal motion approximates horizontal speed.
properties: Integrated range is nondecreasing for nonnegative time steps.

algorithms.name: Geocentric and Geodetic Flight-Path-Angle Rates
algorithms.summary: Compute heading and vertical flight-path-angle rates from acceleration components and coordinate-frame angular velocities.
steps: Express velocity-frame angular velocity as the sum of ECFC-to-local and local-to-velocity rates.
Project angular velocity into velocity-frame y and z directions.
Differentiate the velocity vector in the rotating velocity frame to relate acceleration to frame angular velocity.
Equate corresponding components and solve for vertical flight-path and heading rates.
Repeat with geocentric basis substitutions for geocentric rates.
edge_cases: Heading-rate equation is singular when cos(vertical flight-path angle) is zero.

unit: Check straight constant-velocity flight gives expected coordinate-curvature rates.
properties: Compare with finite differences of recovered flight-path angles.

algorithms.name: Specific Load and Body-Axis Load Factors
algorithms.summary: Compute specific load from inertial acceleration minus gravity or from aerodynamic and propulsive forces, then project it into the body frame.
steps: Compute specific load from either equivalent definition.
Project the vector onto body x, y, and z axes.
Compute total magnitude and lateral magnitude from components.

properties: Force-based and acceleration-minus-gravity definitions agree.
Component norm equals total magnitude.

algorithms.name: Acceleration Contribution Decomposition
algorithms.summary: Combine aerodynamic, propulsive, and gravitational force accelerations with rotating-frame terms to obtain the vehicle acceleration used by the equations of motion.
steps: Sum all external force vectors.
Divide by mass.
Add the Coriolis and centrifugal rotating-frame terms.
Return the acceleration supplied to state-derivative assembly.

properties: Combined result equals the independently assembled equation 2-175 terms.

algorithms.name: Atmosphere Model Setup and Layer Precomputation
algorithms.summary: Select the requested atmosphere model, load layer-base data, and precompute pressure values needed for repeated trajectory evaluations.
outputs: prepared atmosphere model with layer-base pressure, molecular temperature, and molecular weight data
steps: Select the source tables for the requested atmosphere model.
Compute model-latitude reference gravity and effective geopotential radius.
Walk the layers from sea level upward and compute pressure at each layer base.
Store layer data for fast lookup during integration.

unit: Check model selection and layer count.
regression: Verify standard sea-level values for the 1976 atmosphere.

algorithms.name: Reference Gravity and Geopotential Altitude
algorithms.summary: Compute latitude-dependent sea-level gravity, effective geopotential Earth radius, inverse-square gravity, and geopotential altitude.
assumptions: Atmosphere calculations use the model latitude, not the instantaneous trajectory latitude.
steps: Evaluate Lambert's latitude-dependent sea-level gravity equation.
Compute the effective Earth radius used by the atmosphere model.
Apply inverse-square gravity variation with geometric altitude.
Integrate the gravity ratio to obtain geopotential altitude.

unit: Check 45.5425-degree reference values.
properties: Geopotential altitude approaches geometric altitude near sea level and grows more slowly at high altitude.

algorithms.name: Layered Atmosphere Thermodynamic Properties
algorithms.summary: Evaluate molecular temperature, molecular weight, physical temperature, pressure, density, speed of sound, and kinematic viscosity inside an atmosphere layer.
steps: Locate the atmosphere layer containing the requested altitude.
Linearly update molecular temperature from the layer-base gradient.
Interpolate or evaluate molecular weight and convert molecular to physical temperature.
Evaluate pressure with the isothermal exponential formula or nonzero-gradient power law.
Use the perfect-gas relation for density.
Compute speed of sound and Sutherland kinematic viscosity.
edge_cases: Use the correct pressure branch when molecular-temperature gradient is zero.
Reject temperatures or densities outside physical range.

unit: Check isothermal and nonisothermal layer formulas.
properties: Pressure and density remain continuous at layer boundaries.
Pressure decreases with altitude in valid layers.

algorithms.name: High-Altitude Atmosphere Interpolation
algorithms.summary: Evaluate atmosphere properties above 146 km from the 1976 standard high-altitude table using linear temperature and exponential pressure/density interpolation through 1000 km.
steps: Bracket altitude between neighboring high-altitude table rows.
Linearly interpolate temperature.
Interpolate the logarithms of pressure and density, then exponentiate.
Return properties through the 1000-km model limit.
edge_cases: Altitude below 146 km should use the layer equations.
Behavior above 1000 km must be explicitly defined by the new implementation.

properties: Exact values at table nodes.
Positive pressure and density between nodes.

unresolved_questions: The manual does not specify extrapolation behavior above 1000 km.

algorithms.name: Axial and Normal Aerodynamic Force Conversion
algorithms.summary: Convert axial and normal aerodynamic coefficients to a force vector using the body x axis and the windward-meridian direction.
steps: Project the wind x axis into the body y-z plane to form the windward-meridian unit vector.
Apply axial force opposite the body x direction.
Apply normal force opposite the windward-meridian direction.
Scale both components by dynamic pressure and reference area.
edge_cases: At zero total angle of attack, set normal force to zero because the windward-meridian direction is singular.

unit: Check zero-angle axial-only force.
properties: Force magnitudes equal coefficient times q times area.

algorithms.name: Lift, Drag, and Side-Force Conversion
algorithms.summary: Convert lift, drag, and side-force coefficients to a force vector in the wind coordinate system.
steps: Apply drag opposite wind x.
Apply side force along wind y.
Apply lift opposite wind z.
Scale and sum the components.

unit: Check isolated lift, drag, and side-force cases.
properties: Component signs follow the manual convention.

algorithms.name: Body-Axis Aerodynamic Force Conversion
algorithms.summary: Convert body-axis force coefficients CX, CY, and CZ to a force vector.
steps: Form the coefficient-weighted linear combination of body x, y, and z unit vectors.
Scale by dynamic pressure and reference area.

unit: Check each isolated body-axis coefficient.
properties: Force transforms consistently to and from body components.

algorithms.name: Aerodynamic Table Evaluation and Force Accumulation
algorithms.summary: Evaluate one or more aerodynamic coefficient sets, normalize them to wind-axis forces, sum them, and transform the total to ECFC for the equations of motion.
steps: Evaluate each configured coefficient set and reference area.
Convert each set to wind-axis lift, drag, and side force.
Accumulate total wind-axis force components.
Transform the total force to ECFC.
Populate output coefficients according to the source-type availability rules.
edge_cases: Mixed coefficient types yield correct force totals but some coefficient outputs are undefined or partial.

unit: Check accumulation of multiple same-type *aero blocks.
properties: Mixed source coefficient systems produce the same total force when physically equivalent.

algorithms.name: Propulsive Force Vector and Accumulation
algorithms.summary: Construct body-frame thrust vectors from magnitude and two thrust-vector angles, transform them to ECFC, and accumulate multiple propulsion sources.
steps: Resolve each thrust magnitude into body x/y/z components from epsilon1 and epsilon2.
Transform each body-frame vector to ECFC.
Vector-sum all propulsive forces.
Report the sum of magnitudes and the angles from the last evaluated source, matching TAOS behavior.
edge_cases: The reported total thrust magnitude has physical meaning only when all thrust vectors are aligned.

unit: Check zero-angle thrust along body x.
Check orthogonal angle cases.
properties: Each individual vector norm equals its thrust magnitude.

algorithms.name: Geopotential Spherical-Harmonic Expansion
algorithms.summary: Evaluate the Earth geopotential from point-mass, zonal, and longitude-dependent spherical-harmonic terms.
assumptions: TAOS retains terms only through degree four.
steps: Evaluate the point-mass GM/r term.
For degrees two through the configured maximum, evaluate associated Legendre functions.
Accumulate cosine and sine longitude terms by order.
Optionally restrict the sum to zonal harmonics and use Jn = -Cn0.

unit: Check point-mass-only and J2-only reductions.
properties: Potential scales as inverse radius for point-mass model.

algorithms.name: Associated Legendre Function Evaluation
algorithms.summary: Evaluate unnormalized associated Legendre functions used by the degree-four TAOS gravity model.
assumptions: Only degrees through four are required for TAOS.
steps: Evaluate the order-zero Legendre polynomial derivative definition.
Apply the cos(latitude)^m multiplier for associated order m.
Use explicit low-degree expressions or a stable recurrence through degree four.

unit: Verify the printed P1,0 through P4,0 expressions.
properties: Compare recurrence and explicit-polynomial results.

algorithms.name: Spherical-Harmonic Normalization Conversion
algorithms.summary: Convert normalized published spherical-harmonic coefficients to the unnormalized form used internally by TAOS.
outputs: unnormalized coefficient or normalized Legendre value
steps: Compute the degree/order normalization scale factor.
Multiply Legendre functions by the scale factor when normalizing.
Multiply coefficients by the inverse scale factor when unnormalizing.

properties: Normalizing then unnormalizing returns the original value.

algorithms.name: Degree-Four Spherical-Harmonic Gravity Acceleration
algorithms.summary: Compute geocentric gravity-acceleration components as the gradient of the spherical-harmonic geopotential through degree four.
outputs: gravity acceleration vector in geocentric and ECFC components
steps: Evaluate radial, latitudinal, and longitudinal partial derivatives of the geopotential.
Convert derivatives to geocentric north/east/down acceleration components with the documented signs.
Evaluate harmonic sums through degree four.
Transform the geocentric acceleration vector to ECFC.
edge_cases: Longitude terms become numerically delicate near the poles.

unit: Check point-mass reduction when all harmonic coefficients vanish.
properties: Acceleration approximates the negative numerical gradient of potential.
regression: Check WGS-84-full and GEM-T1 coefficient cases.

algorithms.name: J2-Only Gravity Acceleration
algorithms.summary: Compute the simplified point-mass plus J2 gravity acceleration used by the standard WGS-72 and WGS-84 Earth models.
steps: Evaluate north/south gravity correction proportional to sin(latitude) cos(latitude).
Set the east component to zero.
Evaluate radial/down acceleration with the J2 latitude correction.
Transform to ECFC if needed.

unit: Check equator and pole signs.
properties: Reduces to point-mass gravity as J2 approaches zero.

algorithms.name: On-Demand Output-Variable Dispatch
algorithms.summary: Determine which expensive derived output models must be evaluated based on references in print lists, final conditions, expressions, searches, and optimization constraints.
outputs: set of derived-variable evaluators required at each integration point
steps: Collect variable names referenced by output, event, expression, search, survey-summary, and optimization constructs.
Resolve dependencies among derived variables.
Construct an evaluation plan that avoids unused calculations.
Evaluate requested models in dependency order at each required state point.

unit: Verify unused expensive outputs are omitted.
properties: Adding a derived-variable reference adds all transitive dependencies exactly once.

algorithms.name: Sodano Inverse Ellipsoidal Geodesic
algorithms.summary: Compute ellipsoidal surface distance and forward/backward azimuths between two longitude/geodetic-latitude points without iteration.
inputs: longitude and geodetic latitude of two surface points
steps: Convert geodetic latitudes to the auxiliary beta angles.
Evaluate central-angle terms and flattening corrections.
Compute the ellipsoidal surface distance from equations 2-221 through 2-225.
Evaluate corrected longitude and latitude differences.
Compute forward and backward azimuths from equations 2-226 through 2-230.

unit: Check coincident, equatorial, meridional, and short-distance cases.
properties: Distance is symmetric.
Forward/backward solutions agree with sodano_direct round trips.
regression: Compare representative values to a modern ellipsoidal geodesic library while preserving TAOS equations.

unresolved_questions: Document numerical behavior near antipodal configurations, which the manual does not discuss.

algorithms.name: Downrange and Crossrange Projection Search
algorithms.summary: Find the point on a reference azimuth whose connecting geodesic to the vehicle is perpendicular, yielding downrange and crossrange.
steps: Initialize an estimate of downrange along the reference azimuth.
Use Sodano direct to compute the projection point and backward azimuth to the reference.
Use Sodano inverse to compute forward azimuth and distance from projection point to vehicle.
Form the perpendicularity error as the difference between the azimuth separation and 90 degrees.
Update downrange with Newton-Raphson using a forward-difference derivative until the error is within tolerance.
Assign crossrange sign from the orientation of the vehicle relative to the reference azimuth.
edge_cases: Reference curve projection may be nonunique over very long distances.

unit: Check a point exactly on the reference azimuth and a small perpendicular offset.
properties: Projection azimuths differ by 90 degrees at convergence.

algorithms.name: Sodano Direct Ellipsoidal Geodesic
algorithms.summary: Compute destination longitude, geodetic latitude, and backward azimuth from a start point, forward azimuth, and surface distance.
steps: Compute auxiliary latitude and eccentricity terms.
Evaluate the corrected angular distance phi from the series expression.
Compute destination auxiliary latitude and convert it to geodetic latitude.
Compute longitude correction and destination longitude.
Compute the backward azimuth from the destination to the start.
edge_cases: Source equation 2-239 contains inconsistent printed forms; follow the documented editorial resolution in the reconstructed manual.

properties: Direct followed by inverse reproduces distance and azimuth within tolerance.
edge_cases: Zero distance, pole crossing, longitude wrap.

notes: Preserve a traceable implementation decision for the source inconsistency in equation 2-239.

algorithms.name: Radar Observation Geometry and Derivatives
algorithms.summary: Compute radar range, azimuth, elevation, their first and second derivatives, and vehicle aspect and meridional angles from a fixed geodetic radar station.
steps: Build the radar local geodetic basis and ECFC station position.
Form vehicle-relative position and line-of-sight unit vector.
Recover range, azimuth, and elevation from local projections.
Differentiate the range and line-of-sight unit vector for range rate and acceleration.
Evaluate azimuth and elevation first and second derivatives.
Project line of sight into the body frame to compute aspect and meridional angles.
edge_cases: Aspect meridian undefined when line of sight aligns with body x.

unit: Check stationary target and simple local-axis motions.
properties: Range derivatives agree with finite differences.
LOS unit vector remains normalized.

algorithms.name: Relative Vehicle Observation Geometry
algorithms.summary: Compute relative range, body-frame azimuth/elevation, body-axis position components, and closure velocity between vehicles.
steps: Subtract current position from target position.
Normalize the relative vector and compute its range.
Project relative position onto body axes for Cartesian offsets.
Recover body-frame azimuth and elevation.
Project relative velocity onto line of sight for closure velocity.
edge_cases: Body-frame rates are intentionally not computed because guidance attitude can jump instantaneously.

unit: Check target on each body axis.
properties: Relative range is symmetric, while body-frame angles depend on current vehicle attitude.

algorithms.name: Initial Impact Point Ballistic Derivatives
algorithms.summary: Evaluate the simplified ballistic equations of motion used during initial-impact-point propagation, with gravity and constant-ballistic-coefficient drag but no propulsion.
steps: Evaluate gravity at the current IIP state.
Evaluate atmosphere and wind-corrected velocity.
Compute drag acceleration from density, speed, and ballistic coefficient using equations 2-266 through 2-270.
Set propulsion acceleration to zero.
Assemble rotating-Earth position and velocity derivatives.
edge_cases: The printed drag sign depends on the historical TAOS velocity-axis convention; preserve and test the chosen convention explicitly.

unit: Check vacuum ballistic propagation and nonzero-drag deceleration.
properties: Drag changes kinetic energy in the intended direction under the adopted convention.

algorithms.name: Fehlberg Adaptive Runge-Kutta 4/5 Integration
algorithms.summary: Integrate the IIP trajectory with embedded fourth- and fifth-order Runge-Kutta estimates, adapting step size to keep local error within the documented range.
steps: Evaluate the Fehlberg embedded stage derivatives.
Compute fourth- and fifth-order state estimates.
Estimate local integration error from their difference.
Reject and reduce the step when error exceeds 0.01 ft.
Accept and optionally increase the step when error is below 0.001 ft.
Clamp step size to the documented 0.5- to 60-second range.

unit: Integrate benchmark ODEs with known solutions.
properties: Tighter error bounds reduce global error and accepted step sizes.
edge_cases: Step rejection at minimum step and growth at maximum step.

unresolved_questions: The manual cites Fehlberg but does not print the exact embedded tableau; select and document the historical variant used.

algorithms.name: Initial Impact Point Propagation and Output
algorithms.summary: Propagate a ballistic trajectory from the current state to the requested impact altitude, then compute impact coordinates, time, range, and azimuth.
steps: Copy the current vehicle state into an isolated IIP state.
Integrate with adaptive RKF45 until the geodetic altitude crosses the impact altitude.
Refine the terminal step to the impact surface.
Convert terminal ECFC position to geodetic longitude and latitude.
Use Sodano inverse from the tangent-plane origin to compute range and azimuth.
edge_cases: No impact within allowed propagation time.
Initial state already below impact altitude.

properties: Terminal altitude matches requested impact altitude within tolerance.
regression: Reproduce the manual's qualitative ballistic-reentry IIP behavior.

algorithms.name: Ballistic Coefficient and Lift-to-Drag Ratio
algorithms.summary: Compute reentry ballistic coefficient and aerodynamic lift-to-drag ratio from weight, coefficients, and reference area.
steps: Compute ballistic coefficient as weight divided by CD times reference area.
Compute lift-to-drag ratio as CL divided by CD.
edge_cases: CD equal to zero is singular.

unit: Check coefficient cancellation identity in equation 2-272.

algorithms.name: Maximum Lift-to-Drag Angle Search
algorithms.summary: Find the angle of attack that maximizes lift-to-drag ratio using a golden-section search robust to discontinuities.
outputs: angle of attack at maximum L/D
steps: Define the objective as negative lift-to-drag ratio versus angle of attack.
Apply bounded golden-section minimization.
Return the best angle and corresponding positive L/D.

unit: Check a smooth quadratic-like L/D curve.
properties: Returned value is no smaller than sampled neighboring values within tolerance.

algorithms.name: Guidance Rule Classification and Control-Set Selection
algorithms.summary: Classify direct and indirect guidance rules, select the lowest-numbered compatible body-attitude control set, and identify free controls for iterative solution.
steps: Identify rules that directly specify control variables.
Compare their variables with the nine valid attitude sets.
Select the lowest-numbered set containing all directly specified controls.
Set unspecified controls in that set as free variables, defaulting unused controls to zero.
Associate each indirect rule with its preferred solution variable and candidate controls.
edge_cases: Inconsistent directly specified controls are an input error.
Intercept and proportional-navigation rules consume two attitude-control degrees of freedom.

unit: Exercise all nine valid attitude sets and invalid mixed sets.
properties: Selected set is the lowest-numbered compatible set.

algorithms.name: Iterative Guidance Loop
algorithms.summary: Iteratively vary free control variables, recompute attitude, forces, accelerations, and rates, and drive indirect guidance residuals to zero.
steps: Initialize free controls from mid-bounds at the first trajectory point or the previous point's solution thereafter.
Construct body attitude and aerodynamic angles from the current control estimate.
Evaluate aerodynamic and propulsive forces, acceleration, state rates, and guidance solution variables.
Compute residuals between desired and actual solution-variable values.
Use the multidimensional Newton-Raphson solver to update free controls within limits.
Repeat until residuals converge or a failure criterion is reached.

unit: Solve one-control and multi-control synthetic systems.
properties: Converged residual norm is within tolerance and controls remain within limits.

algorithms.name: Parabolic Guidance Transition
algorithms.summary: Fit a quadratic transition from a current first-integral state to a desired state and derivative over the guidance time constant, then return the desired instantaneous derivative.
outputs: desired current derivative or acceleration-like solution variable
steps: Define a quadratic state history through the current value and desired terminal value/derivative.
Solve coefficients a and b from equations 2-275 and 2-276.
Evaluate the first derivative at the current time.
Return it as the desired guidance solution variable.
edge_cases: dtguid must be positive and not too small for stable guidance behavior.

unit: Check endpoint value and derivative constraints.
properties: Correction approaches zero as current state approaches desired steady state.

algorithms.name: Cubic Guidance Transition
algorithms.summary: Fit a cubic transition through current and desired values and first derivatives, then return the desired second derivative at the current time.
steps: Define a cubic state history through the current value/rate and desired terminal value/rate.
Solve b from equation 2-279.
Solve a from equation 2-280.
Evaluate the second derivative 6at + 2b at the current time.

unit: Verify all four boundary conditions.
properties: Returns zero acceleration at an already matched constant state.

algorithms.name: Multidimensional Newton-Raphson Control Solve
algorithms.summary: Solve the nonlinear guidance residual system for free control variables using a numerically estimated Jacobian and Gaussian elimination.
steps: Evaluate the residual vector at the current control estimate.
Perturb each free control and estimate each Jacobian column numerically.
Solve J delta_x = -residual by Gaussian elimination.
Apply the update while enforcing control bounds.
Repeat until residuals meet tolerance or iteration limits are reached.

unit: Solve linear and nonlinear two-variable systems.
properties: Quadratic local convergence for smooth well-conditioned cases.
edge_cases: Singular Jacobian and bounded infeasible solution.

algorithms.name: Predictive Intercept Guidance
algorithms.summary: Assume nonaccelerating interceptor and target motion, estimate time and position of intercept, and command geodetic flight-path angles toward that point.
inputs: interceptor and target positions and velocities
outputs: desired geodetic heading and flight-path angle
steps: Compute relative position and velocity.
Estimate time to intercept as relative distance divided by relative speed magnitude.
Extrapolate the target position linearly to that time.
Construct the line from interceptor to predicted intercept point.
Convert that line to desired geodetic flight-path angles.
edge_cases: Negative or physically implausible intercept time.

unit: Check constant-velocity crossing trajectories.
properties: Predicted positions coincide under the assumed motion model.
edge_cases: Parallel equal velocities and receding target.

algorithms.name: Proportional Navigation Guidance
algorithms.summary: Compute line-of-sight yaw and pitch rates, closure velocity, and commanded normal accelerations proportional to those rates, then transform commands to ECFC guidance targets.
steps: Form relative position and velocity.
Recover line-of-sight yaw and pitch.
Differentiate the angle definitions to obtain LOS rates.
Project relative velocity onto LOS to obtain closure velocity.
Compute yaw and pitch normal-acceleration commands using N' times closure velocity times LOS rate.
Transform commands from LOS coordinates to ECFC.
Convert ECFC acceleration commands to desired flight-path-angle rates for the guidance loop.

unit: Check zero LOS rate gives zero command.
properties: Commanded acceleration is perpendicular to LOS in the modeled frame.

algorithms.name: Range-Insensitive Axis Search
algorithms.summary: Find the body-axis direction of a fixed 10 ft/s delta-v that changes impact time while preserving the aerodynamic-free initial impact point.
outputs: body yaw and pitch defining the range-insensitive axis
steps: Compute the baseline aerodynamic-free impact range and azimuth.
Parameterize a 10 ft/s delta-v direction with yaw and pitch.
Apply the trial delta-v and recompute the aerodynamic-free IIP.
Form range and azimuth residuals relative to the baseline impact point.
Use multidimensional Newton-Raphson to drive both residuals to zero.
Choose the solution branch that increases or decreases time to impact.
edge_cases: No converged solution near the initial guess.

properties: Perturbed IIP range and azimuth match baseline within tolerance while impact time changes.

algorithms.name: Flight-Path Limit Arbitration
algorithms.summary: Apply limits either as Newton bounds on free controls or as replacement guidance rules when flight-condition limits are exceeded.
steps: Ignore a limit on a control that is explicitly specified by guidance.
Apply a control limit as a bound when that control is free.
Compare flight-condition variables against active limits each integration step.
When exceeded, choose the highest-priority associated control and replace its current guidance rule with the limiting rule.
edge_cases: Multiple limits exceeded simultaneously require deterministic priority.

unit: Check specified-control ignore behavior and free-control bounds.
properties: Effective rules enforce the active limit after transition.

algorithms.name: One-Dimensional Newton-Raphson Root Search
algorithms.summary: Iteratively solve f(x)=0 from an initial estimate using a forward-difference derivative and bounded updates.
steps: Evaluate f at the current estimate.
Estimate df/dx with a forward difference.
Update x by subtracting f divided by the derivative.
Restrict the update to the search interval.
Repeat until residual is within tolerance.

unit: Solve linear, quadratic, and transcendental roots.
properties: Quadratic local convergence with exact-like derivative behavior.
edge_cases: Zero derivative and no root in bounds.

algorithms.name: Bracketed Secant Root Search
algorithms.summary: Solve a bracketed root using linear interpolation between opposite-sign endpoints and retain the subinterval containing the sign change.
inputs: lower and upper bounds with opposite-sign values
assumptions: Endpoint function values have opposite signs.
steps: Compute the linear-interpolation root estimate from endpoint values.
Evaluate the function at the estimate.
Replace the endpoint having the same sign as the new value.
Repeat until residual is within tolerance.

properties: Root remains bracketed after each update.

algorithms.name: Parabolic Root Search
algorithms.summary: Fit a quadratic through three function evaluations, select an in-bounds root, discard the least useful point, and iterate to a function root.
steps: Evaluate the function at x-dx and x+dx.
Use a linear estimate for the third startup point.
Fit quadratic coefficients a, b, and c through the three points.
Compute both polynomial roots and choose the valid root closest to the current best estimate.
Evaluate the function there and discard the point farthest from the best root estimate.
Repeat until the function residual is within tolerance.
edge_cases: Both or neither roots in bounds.

unit: Solve exact quadratic roots and mildly nonlinear roots.
edge_cases: Linear degeneration and complex fitted roots.

algorithms.name: Golden-Section Minimization
algorithms.summary: Minimize a bounded one-dimensional function without derivatives by repeatedly discarding a golden-ratio subinterval.
steps: Place two interior points using the golden-section ratio.
Evaluate the function at both points.
Discard the outer subinterval on the side with the larger function value.
Reuse one interior evaluation and compute only one new point.
Repeat until interval width is within tolerance.

unit: Minimize smooth convex and piecewise-continuous functions.
properties: Interval width contracts by the golden ratio.
edge_cases: Minimum at a boundary and flat minima.

algorithms.name: Parabolic Minimization
algorithms.summary: Fit a quadratic through three function evaluations, evaluate its stationary point, and update the three-point interval until predicted and actual minima agree.
steps: Create the same three-point startup set used by parabolic root search.
Fit a quadratic through the points.
Compute stationary point -b/(2a).
Verify the fit represents a minimum and choose a revised interval that retains low function values.
Evaluate the function at the candidate and repeat until fitted and actual values agree within tolerance.
edge_cases: Fitted maximum or nearly zero quadratic coefficient.

unit: Minimize exact quadratics and smooth nonquadratic functions.

algorithms.name: TAOS Nonlinear Programming Problem Construction
algorithms.summary: Construct the objective, equality constraints, inequality constraints, parameter vector, bounds, and scaling for a TAOS optimization loop.
steps: Collect ordered optimization parameters and their initial values/bounds.
Build the objective callback from the requested segment-end expression.
Build equality and inequality constraint callbacks in the documented order.
Apply objective and constraint reference-factor scaling.
Expose a trajectory-evaluation callback that recomputes only affected history.

unit: Construct unconstrained, equality-constrained, and inequality-constrained problems.
properties: Parameter ordering and constraint ordering match problem input.

algorithms.name: Han-Powell Recursive Quadratic Programming
algorithms.summary: Solve the nonlinear program by iteratively constructing an active-set quadratic subproblem, computing a search direction with a positive-definite variable metric, and performing a penalty-function line search.
steps: Select the active set containing all equality constraints and currently active inequalities.
Build the quadratic objective model and linearized active constraints.
Solve the quadratic subproblem for a parameter search direction.
Perform a one-dimensional penalty-function search along that direction.
Update the variable-metric matrix and active set.
Repeat until objective/constraint convergence or failure criteria are met.

properties: Converged active constraints satisfy KKT conditions within tolerance.
regression: Validate against standard constrained-optimization benchmarks and any obtainable vf02ad reference results.

unresolved_questions: The manual gives an overview but not the full vf02ad source algorithm; obtain or independently reimplement the referenced method.

algorithms.name: Path-Integrated Optimization Constraint Variables
algorithms.summary: Represent trajectory-wide inequality violations as nonnegative user-defined integral states for use as endpoint optimization constraints.
steps: Define a nonnegative rate that is zero when the limit is satisfied and positive when violated.
Append the variable to the trajectory state and integrate it over time.
Constrain the final integral to zero in the optimization problem.

unit: Check zero integral for always-satisfied paths and positive integral for violations.
properties: Integral is nondecreasing for nonnegative violation rate.

algorithms.name: Forward and Central Numerical Gradients
algorithms.summary: Estimate objective, constraint, search, and guidance derivatives by forward or central finite differences with configurable increments.
steps: Evaluate the base function when using forward differences.
Perturb each variable by its configured increment.
Use one-sided differences for forward mode or symmetric plus/minus evaluations for central mode.
Assemble scalar gradients or vector-function Jacobians.
edge_cases: Increment too small causes cancellation; too large causes truncation error.

unit: Differentiate polynomials and vector functions with analytic derivatives.
properties: Central differences are more accurate than forward differences at the same well-scaled step for smooth functions.

algorithms.name: Trajectory-Shaping Time-Grid Redistribution
algorithms.summary: Periodically restart trajectory-shaping optimization and redistribute control-history time nodes evenly when the optimized final time distorts the grid.
steps: Detect excessive spacing imbalance or a scheduled restart.
Generate evenly distributed interior time nodes between initial and optimized final time.
Interpolate current control history onto the new nodes.
Restart the optimizer from the redistributed parameterization.

properties: New nodes are evenly spaced and preserve endpoints.
Interpolated control history is continuous at restart.

algorithms.name: Main Program Table/Problem/File Loop
algorithms.summary: Process command-line files, load table files once, loop through problem files and problems, compute trajectories and surveys, and write outputs.
steps: Separate command-line arguments into table and problem files.
For each problem file, create its printout destination.
Before the first problem, parse and retain all table files in memory.
Read each problem in the current file into the runtime data structure.
Compute trajectories and write outputs after successful calculation.
Repeat trajectory computation for every survey-value combination.
edge_cases: If execution terminates before trajectory completion, the historical printout may remain empty.

unit: Check ordering of multiple table and problem files.
regression: Execute all complete Chapter 4 fixtures through the modern runtime once available.

algorithms.name: Vehicle, Segment, and Output Runtime Structure Construction
algorithms.summary: Construct the per-problem vehicle collection with initial conditions, linked segment definitions, output histories, and cross-vehicle references.
outputs: runtime problem graph of vehicles, segments, tables, expressions, and output buffers
steps: Allocate one runtime vehicle record per trajectory.
Attach initial-condition specification and ordered segment records.
Resolve table, trajectory, segment, and variable references.
Create storage for requested output histories and integral states.
Initialize active/inactive/completed status flags.

unit: Build single- and multi-vehicle graphs with direct and inherited starts.
properties: All references resolve to canonical runtime objects.

algorithms.name: Synchronized Multi-Vehicle Trajectory Loop
algorithms.summary: Initialize starting vehicles, synchronize active trajectories on a common time step, integrate them separately, handle events and searches, activate dependent vehicles, and continue until all trajectories complete.
outputs: complete state and output histories for all vehicles
steps: Find the earliest directly initialized vehicle and initialize all starts available at that time.
While any trajectory is active or pending, compute the common next time step.
Integrate each active vehicle independently by the common step.
Resolve segment final conditions, segment changes, and trajectory completion.
Dispatch search or optimization restarts at segment endpoints.
Activate newly available dependent trajectories.
Repeat until all trajectories are complete.
edge_cases: Deadlock where pending trajectories depend on unavailable states.

unit: Single trajectory, simultaneous trajectories, and staged vehicle deployment.
properties: All active trajectories share the same time after each accepted step.

algorithms.name: Common Next-Time-Step Selection
algorithms.summary: Select the smallest active integration step and shorten it to land exactly on print intervals and time-dependent guidance-table points.
inputs: active vehicle times and integration steps
steps: Take the minimum configured integration step among active vehicles.
For each active vehicle, compute time to its next print boundary and reduce the step if smaller.
Inspect time-dependent guidance tables and reduce the step to hit the next knot exactly.
Return the smallest positive candidate consistent with numerical tolerance.
edge_cases: Candidate step at or below floating-point tolerance.

unit: Check independent reductions by vehicle step, print interval, and table knot.
properties: Returned step never overshoots any registered boundary.

algorithms.name: Integrate All Active Vehicles One Step
algorithms.summary: Advance each active vehicle separately by the synchronized common step while retaining a pre-step state for event refinement and restarts.
outputs: candidate post-step states and output samples
steps: Snapshot each active vehicle's pre-step state.
Call fixed-step RK4 independently for each vehicle using the same delta_t.
Compute candidate post-step derived outputs needed for events.
Retain enough information to repeat the step with a refined delta_t if an event is crossed.

properties: Vehicle dynamics are independent except through observed states and shared time.
regression: Compare single-vehicle result with isolated integration.

algorithms.name: Segment Final-Condition Detection and Refinement
algorithms.summary: Detect crossed segment-final conditions, isolate multiple events, and repeat the last integration step with secant-refined time until the terminating condition is met within tolerance.
steps: Evaluate each final-condition residual before and after the candidate step.
Identify all crossed conditions.
If distinct events occur in one step, halve the step repeatedly until only the earliest event remains; retain truly simultaneous events together.
Use a bracketed secant search on delta_t, repeating integration from the pre-step state.
Accept the refined state when the condition is within tolerance and perform the associated goto or stop action.
edge_cases: Several events at the same time.

unit: Check one crossing, simultaneous crossings, and distinct crossings in one large step.
properties: Accepted event residual is within tolerance and no earlier event is skipped.

algorithms.name: Search and Optimization Endpoint Dispatch with Partial Restart
algorithms.summary: At a segment endpoint, evaluate registered search/optimization objectives, update input parameters, and restart trajectory computation immediately before the earliest modified input.
steps: Identify objectives or constraints evaluated at the completed segment.
Pass their values to the owning search or optimization algorithm.
If another iteration is required, update the designated input parameters.
Find the earliest trajectory location affected by any changed parameter.
Restore the corresponding checkpoint and discard only invalidated downstream history.

unit: Check restart points for initial-condition, guidance, and late-segment parameter changes.
properties: Unchanged upstream trajectory history is preserved bit-for-bit.

algorithms.name: Dependent Vehicle Activation
algorithms.summary: Activate inactive trajectories when the source trajectory/segment state needed by their inherited initial condition becomes available.
steps: Inspect inactive vehicles for start references to the current trajectory and segment.
Copy or transform the source state according to the *initial specification.
Apply any configured increments or resets at initialization.
Initialize the first segment and mark the vehicle active.
edge_cases: Multiple vehicles start from the same event.
A start reference is never reached.

unit: Check booster separation and target/interceptor staged starts.
properties: Activated state matches the specified source state plus documented modifications.

algorithms.name: Complete Derivative Calculation Pipeline
algorithms.summary: Execute the ordered state conversion, environment, attitude, force, acceleration, guidance, constraint, and output stages required for a derivative evaluation.
steps: Compute coordinate-system unit vectors and state representations.
Compute state rates and gravity.
Compute atmosphere, wind, airspeed, Mach, dynamic pressure, and Reynolds number.
Initialize body attitude and enter the guidance loop.
Within the loop, compute aerodynamic angles, forces, acceleration, flight-path rates, and specific loads.
After guidance convergence, apply rail/sled constraints.
Assemble state derivatives and evaluate remaining requested outputs.
edge_cases: Order must be preserved because later stages depend on earlier derived state.
Guidance may require repeated force evaluations.

unit: Instrument a synthetic state and verify stage ordering and dependency availability.
regression: Compare outputs against independent calls to each component model.

algorithms.name: Table Definition Validation and Storage Layout
algorithms.summary: Validate table identity, type, independent-variable order, monotonicity, dependent-value cardinality, parameters, and extrapolation policy, then prepare an interpolation-ready representation.

source.section_title: Table File Format and Simple Tables

inputs: known table types and state variables
steps: Verify table identification name uniqueness and table-type validity.
Validate the number and order of independent variables, limited to five.
Check each independent axis is strictly monotonic with no duplicates.
Validate dependent-value count against the Cartesian product for square tables.
Validate table parameters such as sref and units for compatible table types.
Store axes, strides, values, extrapolation policy, and user-variable requirements in an interpolation-ready structure.
edge_cases: The historical Orbus example contains a documented duplicate abscissa and should remain a warning fixture.

unit: Use every Chapter 3 complete and fragment fixture.
properties: Valid square tables have dependent count equal to the axis-size product.
edge_cases: Duplicate points, reversed order, wrong axis order, and unsupported parameters.

algorithms.name: N-Dimensional Linear Interpolation and Extrapolation
algorithms.summary: Evaluate simple or embedded square tabulated data as a multilinear function of up to five independent variables, with either linear extrapolation or endpoint clamping.
assumptions: Interpolation and extrapolation are linear in every independent variable.
steps: For each independent axis, locate the bracketing indices in monotonic order.
If outside an axis range, either retain the first/last interval for extrapolation or clamp the query to the endpoint for no-extrap behavior.
Compute the interpolation fraction on each axis.
Accumulate weighted values from the 2^N surrounding corners using the stored axis strides.
Return the multilinear result.

unit: Check one- through five-dimensional affine functions.
properties: Exact at all table knots.
Reproduces any multilinear function exactly.
edge_cases: Descending axes, clamped no-extrap, and linear extrapolation.

algorithms.name: Full-Table Accumulator Evaluation
algorithms.summary: Evaluate a full TAOS table by initializing the table value to zero and executing its ordered math-operation program until end.
steps: Initialize the accumulator to zero and clear per-evaluation storage variables.
Set the instruction pointer to the start operation.
Resolve each operation's operand, if any.
Apply the operation to the accumulator or control flow.
Continue until the end operation and return the accumulator.
edge_cases: Domain errors in logarithm, square root, inverse trigonometric functions, or division.

unit: Run every Chapter 3 full-table snippet and complete fixture through the interpreter.
properties: Straight-line programs agree with direct arithmetic evaluation.

algorithms.name: Full-Table Operand Resolution
algorithms.summary: Resolve an operation operand as a numeric constant, current state variable, user-defined variable, storage variable, or interpolated embedded table value.
steps: Return literal constants directly.
Resolve known state-variable names from the current trajectory context.
Resolve storage variables created during the current table evaluation.
Resolve remaining declared names as user-defined constants supplied by the problem file.
For embedded table calls, evaluate independent expressions and invoke square or skewed interpolation.

unit: Resolve each operand class and precedence of namespaces.
edge_cases: Undefined names and recursive table references.

algorithms.name: Full-Table Math-Operation Dispatch
algorithms.summary: Apply TAOS accumulator operations including arithmetic, inverse arithmetic, powers, limits, trigonometry in degrees, logarithms, sign and absolute-value operations, and accumulator reset.
steps: Dispatch the operation by its canonical opcode.
Apply binary operations with the documented operand order, including idiv and iexp.
Apply unary functions, interpreting angles in degrees.
Apply min/max as lower/upper limiting operations according to the manual wording.
Return the updated accumulator or a typed domain diagnostic.
edge_cases: Logarithm or square root domain errors.

unit: One test per operation in Table 3-4, including operand-order-sensitive operations.

algorithms.name: Full-Table Storage Variable Semantics
algorithms.summary: Implement csto by saving the accumulator under a unique name and clearing the accumulator for subsequent calculations.
steps: Validate that the storage name does not collide with state or user-defined variables.
Store the current accumulator value under the name.
Set the accumulator to zero.
edge_cases: Duplicate storage definitions should follow a clearly documented overwrite or error policy.

unit: Verify value capture, accumulator clearing, and later operand reuse.

unresolved_questions: The manual requires unique names but does not describe recovery from duplicate csto labels.

algorithms.name: Full-Table If/Label/Goto Control Flow
algorithms.summary: Evaluate simple relational if statements and transfer instruction control to labels using goto operations.
steps: Resolve both relationship operands.
Evaluate exactly one of the supported relations: less than, greater than, or equal.
If true, execute the following math operation or goto; otherwise advance normally.
For goto, replace the instruction pointer with the target label index.

unit: Exercise true/false branches and the complete subsonic/supersonic Chapter 3 example.
edge_cases: Unknown labels and loop budget exhaustion.

algorithms.name: Skewed Tabulated-Data Evaluation
algorithms.summary: Evaluate a tabulated function whose rightmost-axis knots and counts vary across combinations of outer independent variables.
steps: Interpret each group as a one-dimensional table in the rightmost independent variable at one combination of outer variables.
Evaluate the rightmost-axis table for every outer-grid node needed by the query.
Interpolate the resulting values through the remaining outer dimensions in nesting order.
Apply the configured extrapolation policy at each level.
edge_cases: Different rightmost axes and point counts.

unit: Use all three skewed-data examples from Section 3.5.8.
properties: Reduces to square multilinear interpolation when all nested axes are identical.

unresolved_questions: The manual describes data organization but not a unique interpolation order for all possible sparse outer grids; document the chosen recursive semantics.

algorithms.name: Multiple Table Reference Evaluation and Accumulation
algorithms.summary: Evaluate all tables of a requested type active in a trajectory segment and combine their values according to the consuming model, usually by summation.
outputs: evaluated values grouped by table type
steps: Resolve each table identification name to a validated runtime table.
Verify the referenced table type matches the consuming block field.
Evaluate each table in the current context.
Accumulate multiple values using the consuming model's rules, normally scalar or force summation.

unit: Check one and multiple table references and type mismatches.
properties: Evaluation order does not change commutative sums, except documented last-angle output behavior for propulsion.

algorithms.name: User-Defined Expression Evaluation
algorithms.summary: Evaluate trajectory- and problem-level *define expressions over state variables, user variables, temporary variables, table calls, arithmetic, relational operators, and control statements.
outputs: numeric value or updated defined-variable namespace
steps: Resolve literals, state variables, defined variables, indexed vehicle variables, and table calls.
Evaluate unary functions and binary arithmetic with the documented precedence and parentheses.
Evaluate relational conditions and if/else branches where allowed.
Assign results to temporary or output variables in statement order.
Return the final variable values and any diagnostics.
edge_cases: Scope differences between trajectory- and problem-level definitions.

unit: Parameterize over all Chapter 4 define snippets and operators.
properties: Equivalent parenthesized expressions yield expected precedence.
edge_cases: Circular references and undefined indexed trajectories.

algorithms.name: User-Defined Integral Variable Runtime
algorithms.summary: Initialize and integrate user-defined trajectory variables whose derivatives are defined by *define expressions.
outputs: augmented state components and derivative values
steps: Allocate each integral variable as an additional trajectory state.
Initialize it from the definition or documented default.
Evaluate its derivative expression during every derivative call.
Include it in RK4/RKF integration and expose the current value to output and optimization expressions.
edge_cases: Definition references another integral state with ordering dependencies.

unit: Integrate constant and state-dependent derivative definitions.
properties: Integral variables use the same numerical integration stages as physical states.

algorithms.name: Trajectory Initial-Condition Resolution
algorithms.summary: Resolve direct geodetic, geocentric, ECFC, or ECIC initial conditions—or inherit a state from another trajectory/segment—and normalize the result into the ECFC runtime state.
outputs: normalized time, ECFC position/velocity, mass, and auxiliary initial states
steps: Select the declared position and velocity coordinate form.
Validate that a consistent required set of variables is present.
Convert direct position and velocity to ECFC using the coordinate algorithms.
For ECIC input, evaluate the mission-time Earth rotation before conversion.
For inherited input, copy the referenced trajectory state and apply configured overrides.
Initialize mass/weight and other auxiliary state variables.

unit: One valid case for every position/velocity form and inherited state.
properties: Equivalent coordinate forms produce the same ECFC state.
edge_cases: Missing required fields and circular inheritance.

algorithms.name: Increment and Reset State Discontinuities
algorithms.summary: Apply instantaneous state increments, deployment-relative changes, and reset operations at segment boundaries without numerical integration across the discontinuity.
steps: Resolve increment components in the declared coordinate system.
Transform position or velocity increments to ECFC as required.
Apply mass, time, position, velocity, and attitude-related changes atomically.
For reset operations, set path/range/time markers or user variables to their documented base values.
Recompute all derived coordinate and output state after the discontinuity.
edge_cases: Multiple state changes at the same boundary.

unit: Exercise every *increment variable and *reset target in the manual.
properties: Transforms produce frame-independent physical increments.

algorithms.name: *When Final-Condition Evaluation and Action
algorithms.summary: Evaluate ordered segment final conditions, detect crossings, and execute goto or stop actions with the documented priority and initialization behavior.
steps: Evaluate every final-condition expression at segment initialization and at candidate step endpoints.
Convert equality and inequality forms into crossing-aware residuals.
Identify satisfied or crossed conditions in source order.
Select the highest-priority applicable action when multiple conditions are active.
Pass the selected residual to event-time refinement.
edge_cases: Condition already true at segment start.
No fail-safe condition on an unconverged trajectory.

unit: Exercise equality, greater-than, less-than, goto, stop, and indexed-vehicle conditions.
properties: Source-order priority is deterministic.

algorithms.name: *Fly Guidance Rule and Table Resolution
algorithms.summary: Resolve direct, indirect, wildcard, special intercept, and table-valued *fly rules into the control and solution-rule structures consumed by the guidance loop.
steps: Resolve each rule name to a direct control or indirect flight condition.
Replace wildcard values with the previous segment's terminal value.
Resolve numeric values, table references, or special target trajectory numbers.
Validate direct attitude variables form a consistent set.
Build the guidance-rule objects, control priorities, and desired-value evaluators.

unit: Parameterize all direct and indirect guidance rules in Tables 4-2 and 4-4.
edge_cases: Invalid angle sets and first-segment wildcard.

algorithms.name: Survey Value Generation and Cartesian Nesting
algorithms.summary: Generate sorted survey value sets from explicit values or low/high/increment definitions, then iterate all nested combinations in documented survey-number order.
steps: Collect each survey number and all its value specifications.
Expand low/high/increment ranges, including the exact final high value when increments do not land on it.
Merge explicit and generated values, sort them, and remove duplicates according to the documented rule.
Nest surveys in survey-number order and generate every assignment combination.
Substitute assignments into problem parameters before each trajectory run.

unit: Check explicit lists, ascending/descending ranges, merged sets, and nested combinations.
properties: Number of cases equals the product of set cardinalities.

algorithms.name: Search Loop Construction, Nesting, and Execution
algorithms.summary: Build valid independent or nested search-loop topology from *search blocks, bind parameter placeholders and segment-end goals, and drive the configured one-dimensional search method with partial trajectory restarts.
steps: Resolve each search parameter and objective endpoint to a trajectory location.
Build the search dependency intervals and reject intersecting nonnested structures.
Order independent and nested searches from outermost to innermost.
For each search iteration, substitute the parameter, partially recompute trajectory history, and evaluate the endpoint function.
Update the parameter with the configured root or minimization method until tolerance or failure.
edge_cases: Inner search invalidated by outer update.

unit: Validate all structures in Figure 4-11 and reject invalid crossings.
regression: Exercise search snippets from the Chapter 4 corpus.

algorithms.name: Survey Summary Variable Aggregation
algorithms.summary: Accumulate summary variables over each trajectory/survey run using first, last, minimum, maximum, interpolation, and arithmetic operations.
outputs: one summary row per survey case
steps: Initialize each summary accumulator at the start of a survey case.
Evaluate first, last, min, max, or interpolated trajectory values as requested.
Apply subsequent arithmetic and function operations to the accumulator.
Store final summary values with the survey variables and emit the summary row.
edge_cases: Requested interpolation point lies outside trajectory history.

unit: One test per summary operation and chained-operation example.
regression: Reproduce the Ballistic Reentry survey-summary listing.

algorithms.name: *Optimize Block Runtime Mapping
algorithms.summary: Translate *optimize blocks and optX-n placeholders into parameter definitions, objective/constraint callbacks, bounds, finite-difference settings, restart policies, and output controls.
steps: Resolve loop letter and parameter indices to concrete problem input locations.
Apply initial values, lower/upper bounds, scales, and derivative increments.
Resolve objective and constraints to segment-end expressions and reference factors.
Configure forward or central gradient mode, restart behavior, printing, and termination limits.
Produce the callbacks and metadata consumed by the nonlinear optimizer.

unit: Parameterize all optimization variables and options from Table 4-20.
regression: Parse and map the Air-Launched Intercept optimization example.

algorithms.name: Units and Output-Format Resolution
algorithms.summary: Resolve default and overridden units and decimal formats for input and output variables and apply conversions consistently at the problem boundary.
steps: Load each variable's default internal/external unit and decimal precision.
Apply global or per-variable unit and format overrides.
Convert input values from declared units to TAOS internal units.
Convert output values from internal units to resolved display units.
Format values with the resolved width/precision rules.
edge_cases: Precision too wide for output line limits.

unit: One conversion test for every allowable unit family in Table 4-24.
properties: Input-to-internal-to-output round trip within formatting tolerance.

algorithms.name: Wind Input Resolution
algorithms.summary: Evaluate wind magnitude/heading or east/north/down component tables and convert them to the ECFC wind vector used by air-relative velocity calculations.
steps: Evaluate either wind magnitude and heading or east and north components, plus optional down component.
Validate that mutually consistent horizontal representations are used.
Resolve local horizon components in the selected geocentric/geodetic frame.
Transform the local wind vector to ECFC.
edge_cases: Undefined heading for zero horizontal wind.

unit: Check equivalent magnitude/heading and component inputs.
properties: Local-to-ECFC-to-local round trip preserves components.
